summary: Russia launched a massive overnight barrage of 74 missiles and 284 UAVs on July 30, including the first confirmed use of a North Korean ballistic missile that killed a family of five in Radushne, Dnipropetrovsk region. A Russian Kh-101 cruise missile entered Polish airspace near Tarnava-Kolonia, approximately 100 km from the Ukrainian border, prompting Ukrainian fighter interception attempts. Ukrainian air defenses shot down or suppressed 195 enemy UAVs, though 22 strike drones hit 14 locations across the country.
key_points: Russia fired 74 missiles and 284 UAVs overnight July 30, with Ukrainian air defense destroying 195 drones but 22 striking 14 locations. (Source: @UkraineNow/83042)
Zelensky confirmed Russian use of a North Korean ballistic missile in Radushne, killing two parents and three children, with five family members missing. (Source: @UkraineNow/83035)
A Russian Kh-101 cruise missile violated Polish airspace, landing near Tarnava-Kolonia; Polish PM Tusk stated Poland was not the target. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32039)
Russian forces struck Odesa port fuel tanks for AFU and hit a dry cargo ship delivering military cargo south of Odesa. (Source: @tass_agency/387999)
Russian drones attacked three more vessels in the Black Sea operating in Ukrainian interests. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32037)
KAB guided bombs were launched against Zaporizhzhia, Dnipropetrovsk, and Donetsk regions. (Source: @kpszsu/70821)
Jet UAVs were detected across northern and central Ukraine from Chernihiv to Vinnytsia, including toward Kyiv from the northwest. (Source: @kpszsu/70848)
Ukraine's energy grid suffered severe damage in Sumy region with outages in five other oblasts. (Source: @UkraineNow/83021)

sections.executive_summary: Russia conducted its largest combined missile-drone attack of the war on July 30, employing 74 missiles and 284 UAVs including a North Korean ballistic missile that devastated a civilian home in Radushne. A Russian Kh-101 cruise missile penetrated Polish airspace, landing 100 km from the Ukrainian border, while Ukrainian air defenses intercepted 195 drones but recorded 22 strikes on 14 targets. Simultaneously, Russian naval and drone strikes targeted Odesa port infrastructure and Black Sea vessels supporting Ukrainian forces.

points: Ukrainian air defense forces engaged 255 incoming strike UAVs (Shahed, Gerber, Irtlamas, Parody decoys) launched from Orel, Kursk, occupied Donetsk and Crimea, destroying or suppressing 195 drones with aviation, SAM systems, EW units, mobile fire groups and UAV detachments. (Source: @kpszsu/70844)
Ukrainian fighters attempted to intercept Russian missiles heading toward Poland, per Polish Armed Forces Commander General Ireneusz Novak's report to PM Tusk. (Source: @UkraineNow/83032)

SBU detained perpetrators of two July 28 terrorist acts in Odesa: two students recruited via Telegram who planted a remote-detonated device under a military vehicle, and a recidivist who placed explosives under a civilian car detonated by Russian special services, killing the driver and seriously injuring a passenger. (Source: @UkraineNow/83031)

A district TCC operator was caught illegally editing conscript data in the Obereg system for $2,500-$3,000 per person, with 18 individuals using the service to avoid mobilization. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32052)

North Korean ballistic missile used in combat for first time, destroying home in Radushne (Dnipropetrovsk), killing 5 family members, 5 missing. (Source: @UkraineNow/83035)

sections.threat_assessment: Russia has escalated to a new intensity threshold with the debut of North Korean ballistic missiles alongside massive saturation drone attacks, signaling deepening military-technical cooperation with Pyongyang. The Kh-101 incursion into NATO airspace, while likely unintentional, demonstrates degraded Russian missile discipline and raises Article 5 risks. Ukrainian air defense remains effective at high interception rates (76% of 255 UAVs) but leak-through strikes on energy, port infrastructure and civilian areas are degrading societal resilience. The simultaneous multi-axis UAV launches from Russian territory, occupied Crimea and Donbas indicate improved Russian launch coordination and platform standardization. Russian reliance on terrorist recruitment via Telegram for rear-area sabotage suggests a sustained campaign to destabilize Ukrainian rear logistics and morale.
sections.regional_response: Poland confirmed the missile incursion but downplayed intentional targeting, with PM Tusk emphasizing shared threat perception with Ukraine. Ukrainian fighters actively intercepted inbound Russian missiles toward Poland, demonstrating real-time allied air coordination. Bulgaria's nationalization of Lukoil assets reflects growing EU energy security measures against Russian leverage. The EU's €3.47 billion tranche for drones, missiles and fighter jets signals sustained military-industrial support. Trump's hesitation on Patriot production licenses introduces uncertainty in US-Ukraine defense industrial cooperation. Sikorski's historical framing of Polish-Russian confrontation underscores Warsaw's strategic resolve independent of NATO guarantees.
sections.intelligence_notes: The North Korean missile fragments in Radushne provide critical technical intelligence on Pyongyang's ballistic missile performance in combat conditions. Russian use of ZU-23 towed anti-aircraft guns against Ukrainian 'Lyutiy' UAVs indicates layered air defense deployment deep in rear areas. The 'Sky of Odesa' project's rapid fielding of low-cost interceptor drones by mobilized engineers demonstrates Ukrainian asymmetric innovation capacity. TCC corruption via Obereg system manipulation reveals systemic vulnerabilities in mobilization administration exploited at scale ($2,500-$3,000 per evasion). Russian terrorist recruitment via Telegram 'easy money' channels shows effective exploitation of socioeconomic desperation. US uranium enrichment dependence on Russia (26% in 2025) persists despite sanctions, highlighting strategic supply chain fragility.
